extraction_notes: TITLES — the three sources disagree. Résumé: 'Intern – Product Developer' / 'Intern – Software Developer'. LinkedIn export: 'Intern' for both. Earlier Word version: '(AI/ML)' and '(JavaScript)' suffixes. Which wording is on your offer letter or internship certificate?

NUMBERS — 24 numeric claims were added in the Apr28 revision, 18 minutes after the earlier Word version (see numeric_claims[].in_earlier_version). PaySim dataset facts (6.36M rows, 11 features, 0.13% fraud, ~773:1) are properties of a public dataset and can be checked. Claims such as 'accuracy by 25%', '100+ concurrent users', 'sub-second retrieval', '100% formation accuracy', '200+ user interactions' need evidence only you have. Keep the ones you measured; remove or soften the rest.

SKILLS — 16 of 30 listed skills appear in no job or project (evidence_strength: none): C, Flask, Django, NumPy, MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Azure, GitHub, Tableau, Power BI, Excel, VS Code, Postman, Docker, Software Testing. 6 more are weak (an implication or a different meaning). Which can you defend in an interview?

DEGREE NAME — résumé and LinkedIn education say 'Management Information Systems'; the LinkedIn headline says 'MS Information Systems'. The official program name and CIP code on your I-20 decide STEM OPT eligibility, so this is not cosmetic.

TEAM / ROLE — no project states whether it was coursework, team or solo work. The Sphere Soft bullet says '5-member team'. What was your share of each? (A project written as if you led it when you were one of five is the error the assignment names.)
DATES — 'Personal AI Prompter' is dated Jan–Apr 2025. Is it the same project as the Pepper SDD in your Fall 2026 coursework, or a separate earlier one?
